dimensions.name: Evidence-Based Recommendations
dimensions.description: Does output reference 2026 research data and provide evidence for claims?

score_levels.0: No reference to data or research; claims are unsupported
score_levels.1: Mentions data but without specific numbers or unclear sourcing
score_levels.2: References specific 2026 benchmarks (e.g., 6.60% engagement rate, 7-slide optimal)
score_levels.3: Consistently cites research data with specific metrics; explains why recommendations are evidence-based
score_levels.4: Comprehensively grounds all recommendations in 2026 research; provides comparative data (e.g., carousels vs other formats); explains algorithmic reasoning

evaluation_questions: Does output cite specific 2026 metrics (engagement rates, slide counts, timing data)?
Are claims backed by research from the skill's resources?
Does output explain why recommendations work (algorithm logic, user behavior)?
Are benchmarks provided for comparison (e.g., 6.60% is average, your 2% is below)?
Does output reference multiple data sources where appropriate?

dimensions.name: Actionable Specificity
dimensions.description: Are recommendations specific and actionable, or vague and generic?

score_levels.0: Generic advice without specifics (e.g., 'make your hook catchy')
score_levels.1: Some specific guidance but missing details (e.g., mentions slide count without why)
score_levels.2: Specific in most areas (e.g., 'use 7 slides because 18% better than other lengths') but missing some details
score_levels.3: Specific and actionable across all areas (slide count, design specs, timing, hook formula)
score_levels.4: Detailed, step-by-step guidance with examples, templates, and decision trees; covers edge cases

evaluation_questions: Are slide count recommendations specific (e.g., '7 is optimal, range 5-10')?
Are design specs provided (dimensions, fonts, colors)?
Is timing advice specific (day + time, not just 'post during business hours')?
Are hook formulas provided with examples?
Does output provide templates or worksheets?
Are action items numbered/clear (step-by-step workflow)?

dimensions.name: Content-Type Matching
dimensions.description: Does output tailor guidance to the specific content type (framework, narrative, contrarian, etc.)?

score_levels.0: Generic guidance that doesn't account for content type differences
score_levels.1: Acknowledges content type but doesn't adapt guidance accordingly
score_levels.2: Adapts some guidance by content type (e.g., different hook for contrarian vs framework)
score_levels.3: Provides tailored narrative structure, hook formula, and design guidance by content type
score_levels.4: Provides complete content-type-specific playbooks: narrative arc, hook formula, slide structure, typical save rate, CTA approach

evaluation_questions: Does output distinguish between frameworks, narratives, contrarian, data-driven, step-by-step?
Are narrative arcs different by content type?
Are hook formulas tailored (e.g., contrarian hook vs framework hook)?
Does output explain why each content type works (framework = saveable, contrarian = comments)?
Does output provide expected performance (save rate, engagement patterns) by type?

dimensions.name: Problem Diagnosis & Root Cause
dimensions.description: When user reports poor performance, does output identify root causes?

score_levels.0: Doesn't diagnose problem or misidentifies cause
score_levels.1: Identifies one possible cause but doesn't explain why it matters
score_levels.2: Identifies primary cause (e.g., weak hook) and secondary causes (text walls) with explanations
score_levels.3: Comprehensive diagnosis: identifies root cause, explains algorithmic impact, provides evidence
score_levels.4: Diagnostic framework: asks clarifying questions, prioritizes causes by impact, provides testing strategy for verification

evaluation_questions: When user reports low engagement, is root cause identified (hook, text density, CTA)?
Is diagnostic reasoning explained (why this causes the symptom)?
Is algorithmic impact explained (e.g., 'weak hook = algorithm doesn't distribute')?
Does output help user test hypothesis (A/B test, iteration strategy)?
Are secondary causes mentioned if primary cause isn't the issue?

dimensions.name: Workflow Clarity & Completeness
dimensions.description: Are step-by-step workflows clear, complete, and easy to follow?

score_levels.0: No workflow provided or extremely vague
score_levels.1: Workflow provided but with missing steps or unclear sequencing
score_levels.2: Complete workflow with clear steps, but could use more detail or examples
score_levels.3: Step-by-step workflow with all major steps, clear sequencing, and supporting detail
score_levels.4: Comprehensive workflow with: numbered steps, examples, decision points, tools recommended, files needed, checkpoints

evaluation_questions: Is workflow presented step-by-step (numbered or clear sequence)?
Are all major phases included (planning, content, design, technical, quality check, posting, tracking)?
Are tools recommended (Canva, Google Slides, etc.)?
Are checkpoints provided (pre-publication checklist)?
Is there an example or case study walkthrough?
Are decision points clear (choose one narrative arc, choose dimensions, etc.)?

assertion_tests.assertion: Output should reference 2026 carousel engagement benchmark of 6.60% when discussing overall performance
pass_conditions: Contains phrase like '6.60% average' or '6.60% engagement rate'
Or references 'carousel engagement rate' with specific percentage from 2026 data
fail_conditions: No mention of specific engagement rate benchmark
References outdated data (2024 or earlier)

assertion_tests.assertion: Output should explain why 7-slide carousels perform best with reference to 18% improvement metric
pass_conditions: References '18% better' or similar performance comparison
fail_conditions: No mention of optimal slide count
Suggests slide count without evidence
Contradicts evidence (e.g., suggests 12+ slides as optimal)

assertion_tests.assertion: Output should recommend specific dimensions (1080 x 1350px portrait) with explanation
pass_conditions: Explains why (mobile engagement, takes most space, etc.)
fail_conditions: Vague language like 'use portrait orientation' without dimensions
Recommends landscape (wrong)
No mention of dimensions at all

assertion_tests.assertion: Output should specify maximum words per slide (30 words max)
pass_conditions: Provides guidance on what to do if exceeding (split slides)
fail_conditions: Vague: 'keep text short' without number
Wrong number (e.g., '50 words')
No mention of text density guidelines

assertion_tests.assertion: Output should tailor guidance differently for framework vs. contrarian vs. narrative carousels
pass_conditions: When user provides content type, suggests matching narrative structure
Framework carousels: emphasizes named, reusable, saveable
Contrarian carousels: emphasizes data backing, comment-driving
Narrative carousels: emphasizes authenticity, relatable lessons
fail_conditions: Same generic advice regardless of content type
Doesn't acknowledge content type differences
Wrong structure recommended for content type

assertion_tests.assertion: When user reports low engagement, output should identify weak hook as potential primary cause
pass_conditions: Mentions 'hook' in diagnosis of low engagement
References 'hook determines 80% of performance' or similar
Offers specific hook rewrites as solution
fail_conditions: No mention of hook in low-engagement diagnosis
Blames only secondary factors (design, timing) without mentioning hook
Hook mentioned but dismissed as non-critical

assertion_tests.assertion: When user reports text wall issue, output should recommend splitting slides and reference 5-second rule
pass_conditions: Recommends splitting content across more slides
Explains algorithmic impact (dwell time, completion rate)
fail_conditions: No mention of text density as issue
Suggests condensing text instead of splitting
No explanation of why it matters (algorithm impact)

assertion_tests.assertion: Output should provide clear step-by-step LinkedIn upload process
fail_conditions: Workflow missing or out of order
Significant steps omitted
Instructions unclear or contradictory

assertion_tests.assertion: Output should recommend Tuesday-Wednesday and 10 AM-12 PM local time for posting
pass_conditions: Mentions '10 AM' to '12 PM' OR '10-12' time range
fail_conditions: Recommends wrong timing (Monday, Friday, evening)
No specific timing provided
Contradicts research (e.g., 'post whenever you want')

assertion_tests.assertion: Output should emphasize saves as most valuable metric (5x value of likes)
pass_conditions: Mentions 'saves' as primary metric to track
References 'saves are 5x more valuable' or similar
Explains why saves matter (people bookmarking for reference)
Lists metrics in priority order (saves first)
fail_conditions: Emphasizes likes or comments as primary metric
No mention of saves
Treats all engagement equally

assertion_tests.assertion: When discussing fonts, output should recommend 2 fonts max with minimum sizes
fail_conditions: Suggests 3+ fonts
No font size guidance
Font sizes too small (e.g., '18px' for body)
No consistency principle mentioned

assertion_tests.assertion: Output should explain that frameworks are saveable content while contrarian content drives comments
pass_conditions: Framework carousels: 'people save to reference later'
fail_conditions: No distinction between content types in engagement outcomes
Suggests all types drive same engagement

evaluation_notes.what_passes_means: Output demonstrates that the skill is providing high-quality, evidence-based, specific guidance grounded in 2026 research with clear workflows tailored to different carousel types.
evaluation_notes.what_fails_means: Output relies on generic advice, lacks specific metrics/benchmarks, doesn't tailor to content type, or provides incomplete workflows.
typical_issues: Generic advice without specifics (loses points on Actionable Specificity)
No reference to 2026 research benchmarks (loses points on Evidence-Based)
Same guidance for all content types (loses points on Content-Type Matching)
Missing steps in workflows (loses points on Workflow Clarity)
Misidentifies root cause when troubleshooting (loses points on Problem Diagnosis)

how_to_interpret_scores.90-100: Excellent: Comprehensive, specific, data-driven guidance with tailored workflows and problem diagnosis
how_to_interpret_scores.80-89: Good: Specific recommendations with evidence; may lack some depth in tailoring or examples
how_to_interpret_scores.70-79: Acceptable: Addresses key areas; some generic language or missing specifics in certain dimensions
how_to_interpret_scores.60-69: Below Threshold: Lacks evidence, specificity, or tailoring; may have incomplete workflows
how_to_interpret_scores.Below 60: Poor: Fails to meet multiple criteria; doesn't use skill effectively
